subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw core expose a shell-facing admin notification broadcast to connected Control UI sessions, and what auth scope, targeting, payload, delivery, and abuse-control contract should it use?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested surface, but adding it crosses CLI, Gateway protocol, operator authorization, and UI interruption boundaries that automation should not choose implicitly.

options.title: Define a narrow core notify contract
options.body: Add an explicit admin-scoped CLI/Gateway/Control UI notification path with sanitized payloads, targeting rules, abuse controls, docs, and tests.

options.title: Fold into broader WebUI notifications
options.body: Make the broader WebUI notification tracker own the shell/admin Gateway API before closing or merging this issue into that design.

options.title: Defer outside core
options.body: Keep the feature in plugins/hooks or future plugin API work until maintainers decide core should own connected-UI notifications.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core notify contract
recommendation.body: Add an explicit admin-scoped CLI/Gateway/Control UI notification path with sanitized payloads, targeting rules, abuse controls, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the current CLI/Gateway broadcast and operator-scope boundary where current-main history points most strongly to steipete.
